content:
Jules (support): FYI customer 'AMA-500' in APAC hitting lots of 5xx/401s and +250ms tail latency since ~2026-03-16 22:00 UTC. Their traces show requests landing in us-west-2. Suspect DNS/GeoIP routing. Anyone can take a quick look?
Priya (network-sre): Can you paste a failing request (no PII) and the resolved IP from their client resolver? Also which resolver are they using? EDNS/EDNS0?
Jules (support): Here's an example from them (sanitized):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  --trace-ascii - 

Host resolved to: 54.210.11.77\nx-region: us-west-2\nresponse: 401 or sometimes 504\n```

They say their ISP resolver is the local TelcoAP (no EDNS client subnet).
Alejandro (eng-platform): We rolled a Cloudflare LB change for ap-southeast yesterday (reduced healthcheck TTL to 60s and changed failover pools). If the ISP resolver had cached the previous Anycast mapping (or an old A record), traffic could still be steered to the US pool.
Maggie (eng-infra): dns-monitor-bot: health check spikes?
dns-monitor-bot: ap-southeast pool flagged UNHEALTHY at 2026-03-16T21:58:14Z, recovered at 2026-03-16T22:10:26Z — failover to default_pool (us) for ~12m.
Priya (network-sre): That matches. If the CF pool failed, traffic would be routed to default (US). But the weird bit is the customer's resolver is returning an A in the US even after recovery — likely due to ISP caching (long TTL or negative caching).
Alejandro (eng-platform): Also note our auth service is regionalized for dedicated tenants. If requests land in US pool, token issuer checks tenant region and can return 401 if tenant is APAC-only. That explains mixed 401s.
Jules (support): The customer ran `dig @their-resolver api.redwood.example.com` and got the US A. I asked them to try `dig +trace` and `dig @8.8.8.8` — 8.8.8.8 returns APAC IPs. So it's clearly resolver caching at ISP.
Priya (network-sre): Short-term mitigations:
- Ask customer to use 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 or flush their resolver cache (if possible).
- We can reduce TTL to 30s, but that won't clear ISP caches immediately.
- We can roll traffic back to previous LB config (revert change) to reduce flapping.
Alejandro (eng-platform): I'd prefer a targeted roll-back of the healthcheck settings for APAC to avoid further flaps. Also, we can add an explicit geo-steering rule in CF to prefer APAC ASNs/Nets for that pool. That helps ISPs that honor EDNS/ASN.
Maggie (eng-infra): For diagnostics, can we get the customer's resolver IP and TTL value they observed? Also paste a full `dig +short +ttl` output.
Jules (support): They returned: `resolver: 203.45.67.89 (TelcoAP)`, `dig +short +ttl api.redwood.example.com -> 54.210.11.77 (TTL 7200)`. So TelcoAP has a long TTL cached.
Priya (network-sre): 7200s is killer. ISP caches like that mean our changes won't propagate for ~2h. We can't force ISPs to flush. We should:
- Revert healthcheck TTL change and ensure apac pool stays healthy.
- Add a temporary HTTP 307 redirect or region-pinned answer? Not great.
Alejandro (eng-platform): Also a note: rolling IPs to break cache is a last-resort; it causes connection churn but will clear the cached mapping quicker. Coordinate with infra to avoid auth/eval regressions.
Jules (support): Customer tried `curl --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:13.250.12.9` pointing to a known APAC IP and saw latency drop to ~45ms and auth succeed. So that proves it's just landing PoP mismatch.
Maggie (eng-infra): Action items:
- I'm reverting the CF LB healthcheck change (in progress, ETA 10m).
- Alejandro please hold geo-steering rule changes for a follow-up with SRE.
- Priya please document recommended TTL policy for public pools and failover.
- Jules escalate to account team with workaround (use 8.8.8.8 or flush) and note temporary impact window.
Jules (support): I'll send the customer the workaround and ETA. If they can't change resolver, offer a temporary regional ingress DNS name they can `--resolve` or we can open a support tunnel.
Alejandro (eng-platform): Also add an item to postmortem: healthcheck sensitivity + CF failover should not trigger cross-region auth failures. Consider making auth validation tolerant during global failover windows (with strict logging).
Priya (network-sre): Quick repro commands for future:
```
dig @203.45.67.89 api.redwood.example.com +short +ttl
dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com +short +ttl
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:<apac-ip> https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
Jules (support): Thanks team :thumbsup:. I'll update the ticket and close once CF rollback is complete or customer confirms back to APAC.
Maggie (eng-infra): CF rollback completed at 2026-03-16T22:18:40Z. Monitor for 30m.
Priya (network-sre): Noted, I'll follow the monitor. If we still see TelcoAP returning US IPs after 30m, we'll consider IP rotation.
Jules (support): Customer confirmed at 22:35 UTC they see APAC IPs and errors gone. Closing for now, will reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
